The imaging phenotype is classic for glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype: a large, solitary, midline-crossing mass with marked, thick-walled ring enhancement and a significant necrotic core. The presence of extensive vasogenic edema and a relatively sharp tumor-edema boundary further supports this. The absence of a T2-FLAIR mismatch argues against an IDH-mutant astrocytoma. Oligodendrogliomas typically lack the marked ring enhancement, central necrosis, and extensive deep white matter invasion seen in this case. The presence of a large necrotic core and thick, irregular enhancement strongly suggests a non-codeleted phenotype, characteristic of high-grade astrocytic tumors. overall_comment: The patient is a 66-year-old female with a large, midline-crossing frontal mass. The combination of advanced age and imaging features—including marked ring enhancement, central necrosis, and significant mass effect—are pathognomonic for a glioblastoma. All three independent predictions (IDH-wildtype, 1p/19q non-codeleted, and WHO grade 4) are made with very high confidence and are mutually consistent, leading to an integrated diagnosis of Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4.
